title: Matrix exponentials from the power series
subtitle: G2 lecture 039000 · expanded companion
adaptation: Individually authored from the spoken lecture and its display-only mathematical appendix. Includes stepwise constructions, explicit hypotheses, worked examples and topic-specific vector figures; all slide prose is independent of audio.

slides.title: How to build a continuous linear motion
slides.lead: We seek a family of maps that starts at the identity and evolves under one fixed linear rule.
body: A constant matrix B specifies a velocity field x′(t)=Bx(t). The exponential e^{tB} packages the solution for every initial vector simultaneously: x(t)=e^{tB}x(0).
This provides the basic language of linear dynamical systems, flows, shears, and rotations. For a fixed generator the flow for time s followed by time t equals the flow for time s+t.
slides.takeaway: The matrix exponential converts a time-independent generator into a one-parameter flow.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 039000 · How to build a continuous linear motion

slides.title: The series definition
slides.lead: Replace the scalar exponential series by matrix powers.
body: In finite dimensions, the power series converges absolutely in any matrix norm because ||Bⁿ|| ≤ ||B||ⁿ. It therefore defines an operator for every real t, with I as its constant term.
Each higher-order term records repeated applications of the generator. One can differentiate the series term by term on compact time intervals, just as for the scalar exponential.
slides.takeaway: Absolute norm convergence makes the power series a legitimate matrix definition.

slides.title: A nilpotent generator produces a shear
slides.lead: Consider N(x,y)=(y,0). A second application of N is zero.
body: Every term of degree two or higher vanishes, so e^{tN}=I+tN. It sends (x,y) to (x+ty,y): horizontal displacement increases linearly with the vertical coordinate.
For t=1, the square with corners (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1) becomes a parallelogram. The mapping is invertible even though N itself is singular.
slides.takeaway: Exponentiating a nilpotent map produces an invertible shear.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 039000 · A nilpotent generator produces a shear

slides.title: Differentiate the flow
slides.lead: The series solves the differential equation with the correct initial condition.
body: Differentiating tⁿBⁿ/n! gives tⁿ⁻¹Bⁿ/(n−1)!, and reindexing yields B times the original series. Since B commutes with every power of itself, multiplication on the other side agrees.
At t=0 only the constant term remains, so the initial operator is I. Uniqueness of the linear initial-value problem then identifies this construction as the flow generated by B.
slides.takeaway: The derivative identity explains why e^{tB} transports all initial data.

slides.title: Composition and inverse
slides.lead: Running a fixed flow for two successive time intervals adds their durations.
body: The matrices sB and tB commute. Multiplying their exponential series and collecting terms by total degree gives the binomial coefficients for (s+t)B.
Taking the second interval to be −t shows that e^{tB} has inverse e^{−tB}. The generator need not be invertible; the exponential is invertible anyway.
slides.takeaway: A single matrix generator yields a one-parameter group of invertible transformations.

slides.title: Why we cannot combine arbitrary exponentials
slides.lead: The composition identity only used commuting matrices.
body: For two different matrices B and C, the mixed products BC and CB may differ. Then the coefficient of t² in e^{tB}e^{tC} is not generally the coefficient of t² in e^{t(B+C)}.
The formula e^B e^C = e^{B+C} holds when B and C commute, but it is unsafe without that condition. This distinction matters for rotations about different axes.
slides.takeaway: The exponential combines generators by addition only under commutation.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 039000 · Why we cannot combine arbitrary exponentials

slides.title: A skew-adjoint generator preserves lengths
slides.lead: Suppose B* = −B. Then e^{tB} is unitary (orthogonal in the real case).
body: Taking the adjoint of the exponential series gives (e^{tB})*=e^{tB*}=e^{−tB}. The inverse identity then shows (e^{tB})*e^{tB}=I.
Thus every vector keeps its norm under the flow. This is the operator form of a rotation or another length-preserving linear motion.
slides.takeaway: Skew-adjoint infinitesimal motion exponentiates to a unitary flow.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 039000 · A skew-adjoint generator preserves lengths

slides.title: The planar rotation generator
body: Because J²=−I, even powers in the exponential series contribute the cosine series and odd powers contribute the sine series times J.
The resulting flow rotates every vector counterclockwise through angle t. This gives a derivation of the rotation matrix directly from the series, rather than assuming its trigonometric form.
slides.mathtex: e^{tJ}=\cos t\,I+\sin t\,J=\begin{bmatrix}\cos t&-\sin t\\\sin t&\cos t\end{bmatrix}
slides.takeaway: The familiar rotation matrix is an exponential of a skew-symmetric generator.

slides.title: Several independent rotation planes
slides.lead: A block-diagonal generator can rotate different orthogonal planes at different rates.
body: If B acts as ω₁J on one invariant plane and ω₂J on another, then e^{tB} restricts to rotations through angles ω₁t and ω₂t on those planes.

The construction scales beyond the plane: find invariant blocks, exponentiate within each block, and reassemble. It also prepares us to discuss unitary flows and operator-valued trigonometric functions.
slides.takeaway: An orthogonal decomposition turns one flow into independent plane rotations.

slides.title: Reconstruct the two examples
slides.lead: The shear and rotation expose different behaviors of the same series definition.
body: Compute e^{tN} from N²=0 and e^{tJ} from J²=−I. Verify their time-composition laws by multiplying the resulting two-by-two matrices.
Then explain why one family changes lengths but preserves area, while the other preserves lengths. The difference is the generator: N is nilpotent; J is skew-adjoint.
slides.takeaway: The generator determines the type of continuous motion.
